stem:
A 34-year-old G2P1 at 40+3 weeks is having a spontaneous vaginal birth. The head has just delivered but has retracted against the perineum and gentle routine axial traction with the next contraction fails to deliver the anterior shoulder. The registrar is on the way and the midwife has called for help. The mother is in a supine lithotomy position.

The patient's last birth was uncomplicated. Her booking BMI was 34 and her most recent HbA1c at 26 weeks was 42 mmol/mol. The baby is estimated to weigh 4200 g on her most recent scan.

data_table.Vital signs (mother): HR 106, BP 128/78, RR 22, SpO2 98 percent on room air, temp 37.0 C
data_table.History: G2P1, term, spontaneous vaginal delivery of head 30 seconds ago; head retracting against perineum; routine axial traction failed

lead_in: What is the next appropriate manoeuvre?

options.text: Deliberate fundal pressure at the maternal umbilicus with the contraction
options.rationale: Fundal pressure is contraindicated in shoulder dystocia because it worsens shoulder impaction against the pubic symphysis and increases uterine rupture and brachial plexus injury risk. Suprapubic pressure (over the anterior shoulder) is the correct pressure, not fundal. (Source: RANZCOG Shoulder dystocia guideline)

options.text: Zavanelli manoeuvre with cephalic replacement and immediate caesarean section
options.rationale: Zavanelli is a last resort when all other manoeuvres have failed; performing it as first-line abandons the standard algorithm and commits to laparotomy for a dystocia that resolves with simpler measures in most cases. (Source: RANZCOG Shoulder dystocia guideline)

options.text: McRoberts manoeuvre with hyperflexion of maternal hips to the abdomen combined
options.rationale: The AU HELPERR mnemonic and RANZCOG shoulder dystocia algorithm start with H (call for help), E (evaluate for episiotomy - not always required), L (legs into McRoberts hyperflexion). McRoberts plus suprapubic pressure resolves 50 to 60 percent of shoulder dystocia and is always first. (Source: RANZCOG Shoulder dystocia guideline)

options.text: Symphysiotomy of the pubic symphysis with cardiac monitoring with cardiac monitoring throughout
options.rationale: Symphysiotomy is not part of standard AU shoulder dystocia management; it has been abandoned in high-resource settings because of severe maternal morbidity. (Source: RANZCOG Shoulder dystocia guideline)

options.text: Delivery of the posterior arm before McRoberts with cardiac monitoring throughout
options.rationale: Posterior arm delivery is an internal manoeuvre and comes after external manoeuvres (McRoberts plus suprapubic pressure) have been tried. Skipping to internal manoeuvres first raises brachial plexus injury risk unnecessarily. (Source: RANZCOG Shoulder dystocia guideline)

explanation.summary: Shoulder dystocia follows the HELPERR sequence: H (help), E (episiotomy consideration), L (legs into McRoberts hyperflexion with suprapubic pressure), P (posterior arm delivery), E (enter and rotate - Rubin, Woods), R (roll to all-fours Gaskin), R (repeat or Zavanelli). McRoberts plus suprapubic pressure resolves the majority; internal manoeuvres come after external manoeuvres fail.
key_points: First external manoeuvre: McRoberts plus suprapubic pressure (resolves 50 to 60 percent)
Fundal pressure is contraindicated; suprapubic pressure only
Internal manoeuvres (posterior arm, rotation) after external manoeuvres fail
Zavanelli and symphysiotomy are last-resort and rarely used in AU practice
explanation.pearls: Fundal pressure is the exam trap - it worsens impaction, and the correct pressure is suprapubic over the anterior shoulder.
